hero.name: LangGraph Brain Agent
hero.pitch: A business operations agent with human-in-the-loop approvals, crash-safe durable state and a long-term memory "brain".

whatItDoes.title: What it does
whatItDoes.description: An operations assistant for a small team. It acts on email, CRM and tasks, and the rules decide what it may do alone.

email.title: Email
email.text: Reads and drafts messages and sends them on behalf of the team.

crm.title: CRM
crm.text: Looks up contacts and deals and updates records.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.text: Creates, updates and completes tasks, and deletes them when approved.

items.externalEmail: Emails to recipients outside @acme.com, including cc
items.bulkEmail: Bulk emails to more than 5 recipients

graph.title: How a run flows
graph.description: The agent is a LangGraph state graph. Select a node to see what it does and what it guarantees.

load_context.summary: At the start of each user turn, recalls the most relevant long-term memories (semantic search over the store) and adds them to the model context.

guarantees.capped: Recall is capped (5 memories by default)

reason.summary: Calls the model with a system prompt rebuilt from the rule set on every call. If the model asks for tools the run goes to the approval gate; otherwise the turn ends.

guarantees.reload: Rule reloads apply on the next call
guarantees.maxSteps: Bounded by a max-steps limit (25 by default)
guarantees.backoff: Transient errors retried with exponential backoff

approval_gate.summary: Checks every tool call against the approval policy: tool metadata plus the hard rules. Calls that violate a block rule are refused; calls that require approval are marked for review.

await_approval.summary: Pauses the graph with a LangGraph interrupt() until a human approves, edits, rejects or responds to each pending call.

guarantees.checkpointed: The pause is checkpointed in PostgreSQL, so it survives restarts
guarantees.rechecked: Edited calls are re-checked against block rules

resolve_uncertain.summary: Before tools run, asks a human about calls whose earlier execution has an unknown outcome (recorded as started in the tool ledger, but never finished).

guarantees.choice: The human chooses: confirm done, retry or skip
guarantees.onlyUncertain: Only calls that are still uncertain are asked about

tools.summary: Executes the approved tool calls through the tool ledger, keyed by thread id and tool call id, then hands the results back to the model.

guarantees.replayed: Succeeded calls are replayed from the ledger, not re-run
guarantees.atMostOnce: Side effects happen at most once unless a human authorizes a retry

memorize.summary: At the end of a turn, asks the model to extract durable facts and preferences and writes them to the long-term store.

summarize.summary: When the history exceeds the context budget, folds the oldest messages into a running summary so the prompt stays within bounds.

END.summary: The turn is finished. The final state stays checkpointed and the thread can continue.

guarantees.persisted: Every step before this point was persisted

crashSafety.title: Crash safety, step by step
crashSafety.description: What happens when the process dies while an email is being sent.

crashWalkthrough.autoplayDisabled: Autoplay is off because reduced motion is preferred

checkpoint.label: Checkpoint
checkpoint.title: A checkpoint is saved after every step
checkpoint.description: The graph state is written to PostgreSQL before the next step starts (synchronous durability). The run is also registered with a lease that its owner keeps renewing with a heartbeat.

crash.label: Crash
crash.title: The worker crashes mid-tool
crash.description: The process dies while the send_email tool is running. Nothing renews the lease anymore, so it expires. The last checkpoint is intact.

claim.label: Recover
claim.title: A recovery worker claims the orphaned run
claim.description: The recovery worker looks for runs whose lease expired and claims them with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so two workers never take the same run. Each claim bumps a fencing token, which makes a stale owner unable to renew or finish the run.

ledger.label: Ledger
ledger.title: The tool ledger decides what is safe to repeat
ledger.description: Every tool call is recorded under thread id and tool call id. A succeeded call replays its stored result instead of running again. A call left started whose tool is not retry-safe has an unknown outcome, so a human decides: confirm done, retry or skip.

resume.label: Resume
resume.title: The run resumes and the email is sent exactly once
resume.description: The graph continues from the last checkpoint with the ledger as the source of truth. The email is never duplicated: it is either replayed from the ledger or confirmed by a human first.

hitl.title: Human in the loop
hitl.description: Sensitive actions wait for a person. The wait is part of the durable state, not a process held in memory.

pause.label: Pause
pause.text: A sensitive tool call stops the graph at an interrupt().

decision.label: Decision
decision.text: A human approves, edits the arguments, rejects, or responds with free text.

resume.label: Resume
resume.text: The graph continues from the checkpoint with that decision applied.

notes.persisted: Pending approvals live in the PostgreSQL checkpoint, so they survive restarts and deploys.
notes.unknown: An execution whose outcome is unknown (the process died mid-tool) is never guessed: it waits for a human.

confirm.label: Confirm done
confirm.text: The side effect did happen; keep its result.

retry.label: Retry
retry.text: Run the tool again, explicitly authorized by a human.

skip.label: Skip
skip.text: Do not run it; the agent is told it was skipped.

brain.title: The brain
brain.description: Memory, rules and context assembly sit around the loop, so the agent knows what it knows and what it may do.

items.store: Facts, preferences and episodes kept in a PostgreSQL store
items.lifecycle: Recalled at the start of a turn, extracted at the end
items.upkeep: Corrected and updated instead of duplicated; never learns from an email
items.graph: Visible as a knowledge graph: memories, rules, CRM and tasks connected

items.yaml: Persona and guidelines in a YAML rule set
items.hard: Hard rules: block or require approval
items.reload: Hot reload; invalid rules fail closed

items.assembled: The prompt is assembled within a size budget
items.folded: Old messages are folded into a running summary
items.cache: A stable, cacheable prompt; date, user and memories go in a per-turn block
items.untrusted: Emails enter as untrusted content: whatever follows needs approval
items.evals: Context evals in CI: caching, budget, isolation and memory quality

architecture.title: Architecture & stack
architecture.ariaLabel: Architecture: the React UI talks to FastAPI, which drives the LangGraph runtime. The runtime uses PostgreSQL for checkpoints, memory, runs and the tool ledger, and OpenAI for models.

postgres.title: PostgreSQL
postgres.detail: Checkpoints, store + pgvector, runs, tool ledger

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.description: Run the whole stack locally: PostgreSQL in Docker, the backend with uv, the frontend with npm.
